title: Four steps per exam problem (with minutes)
ask: What are the four steps for each 22-minute problem, and how many minutes go to each?
items: Read twice (4 minutes): first for ideas, then slowly; mark actors, powers, exact words, numbers, repeated facts, the question asked.
Analyze and outline (4 minutes): the six questions; two or three issues; decide your conclusion before writing.
Write in CLEAR (11 minutes): about 80–120 legible words in your box on the back of the questionnaire.
Check (3 minutes): R agrees with C; the question asked is answered; every word readable; student number written.
src: Exam method (rule map 00); 1 hr 30 min, four problems, all answers on the back of the questionnaire

title: The CLEAR answer
ask: What do the five letters of CLEAR stand for, and what goes in each?
items: C – Conclusion: the short answer first (‘The expulsion is void.’).
L – Legal basis: the provision and rule; name a case only if you are sure of it.
E – Exception: only if one actually applies; usually omitted.
A – Analysis: apply the law to the specific facts; non-negotiable.
R – Restatement: restate the conclusion; it must agree with C.
src: Essay-exam module Sir Dan shared (Atty. Tanya Lat, UP College of Law)

title: Exam-room rules (Sir Dan, Oct. 2026)
ask: What are Sir Dan’s six exam-room rules, and what is the penalty for breaking one?
items: Identify yourself only by your student ID number; no other identification.
Use the questionnaire as the answer sheet; write at the back; all answers must fit there.
Do not write a dissertation.
No communication with classmates in any manner.
No electronic devices: only a pen and correction tape; nothing else on the table.
Unreadable answers are marked incorrect.
Penalty for any violation: a 5.0 for the exam.
src: Sir Dan’s reminders via the beadle (Oct. 13, 2026)

title: Six questions before you write
ask: What six questions should you answer, in order, before writing an essay answer?
items: What is the question being asked (usually the last sentence)?
What issues are relevant to that question?
Which facts are material, and how do the issues relate to them?
What legal principles apply (provision, doctrine, case)?
How do those principles apply to these facts?
What is my conclusion? Decide it before writing.
hook: Question → Issues → Facts → Law → Apply → Conclude
